evidence_quotes.quote: Como variável dependente, optou-se pela utilização dos dados acerca do atendimento/cobertura de três dos quatro serviços de saneamento básico, a saber: abastecimento de água, esgotamento sanitário e coleta de resíduos sólidos.

Este estudo objetivou compreender se há influência entre a capacidade institucional e os indicadores de acesso aos serviços de saneamento básico em Minas Gerais. Para isso, foram consideradas dez variáveis referentes às questões financeiras, presença de corpo técnico da prefeitura atuando no setor de saneamento, o número de veículos e funcionários atuantes e a existência de plano e política de saneamento no município.
Por fim, as variáveis referentes aos planos e políticas de saneamento foram agrupadas num único fator, denominado Capacidade Política.

Com o auxílio de uma Análise Fatorial Exploratória, essas variáveis foram reduzidas a quatro indicadores de capacidade institucional: política, financeira, técnica e operacional, utilizadas como variáveis explicativas para a execução da regressão linear múltipla.

Os dados revelaram que, na amostra em questão, há um maior acesso ao abastecimento de água (com uma média de 62% de atendimento) e, em menor grau, do esgotamento sanitário (aproximadamente 42% de atendimento).

criterion_notes.c1: Examines municipal household/population water supply and sanitary sewerage service access (alongside solid waste collection) across municipalities in Minas Gerais, Brazil.
criterion_notes.c2: Passes the plain wording of Criterion 2 (plain=yes) because it examines municipal institutional and governance capacities (financial, technical, operational, and political/planning capacity, including binary indicators for whether the municipality has a Municipal Basic Sanitation Plan [PMSB] and Policy [PPSB] under Law 11.445/2007). Fails the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading (narrow=no) because its explanatory variables measure general municipal administrative, fiscal, operational, staffing, and planning capacity (per capita revenues and expenditures, municipal technical staff, waste collection staff/vehicles, and binary existence of a general municipal sanitation plan/policy aggregated via PCA into broad capacity indices) rather than a rule-type mechanism directly governing service access (such as eligibility screening, administrative burden, documentation or tenure requirements, tariff or cost-recovery rules, discretion or accommodation, enforcement, or utility ownership or regulatory structure directly governing service access).
criterion_notes.c3: Quantitative empirical cross-sectional study analysing 2017 IBGE and 2018 SNIS secondary data across Minas Gerais municipalities using exploratory data analysis, ANOVA/chi-square tests, principal components exploratory factor analysis, and OLS multiple linear regression with White robust standard errors (N = 391 in regression models).
criterion_notes.c4: Reports municipal service access/coverage outcomes from SNIS (2018): total water supply attendance index (Atend_Agua, %), total sanitary sewage attendance index (Atend_Esgoto, %), and solid waste collection coverage (Atend_RDO, %).
criterion_notes.c5: Clearly identifies unit of analysis and population (municipalities in Minas Gerais, Brazil; 574 after outlier removal, 391 in regressions), exposures (four PCA-derived institutional capacity scores), outcomes (municipal water, sewage, and solid waste coverage percentages), and study design (cross-sectional quantitative observational regression analysis).
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in Portuguese, which is directly eligible without translation under Criterion 9.

study_design: Cross-sectional quantitative observational study using Exploratory Factor Analysis (principal components with varimax rotation) and Multiple Linear Regression (OLS with White robust standard errors)
population_and_sample: Municipalities of Minas Gerais, Brazil (574 municipalities retained after outlier removal for descriptive analysis; N = 391 municipalities in the final multiple linear regression models)
exposure: Four municipal institutional capacity factor scores extracted via principal components factor analysis from 10 IBGE (2017) and SNIS (2018) variables: Financial Capacity (per capita direct/indirect operating revenues and total/personnel water and sewage expenditures), Technical Capacity (presence of municipal technical staff in water supply and sanitary sewage), Operational Capacity (solid waste employees and vehicles per 10,000 inhabitants), and Political Capacity (binary existence of a Municipal Basic Sanitation Plan [PMSB] and Municipal Public Policy of Basic Sanitation [PPSB] under Law 11.445/2007)
outcome: Municipal service coverage rates in 2018 (SNIS): total water supply attendance index (Atend_Agua, %), total sanitary sewage attendance index (Atend_Esgoto, %), and regular household solid waste collection coverage rate (Atend_RDO, %)
rationale: This quantitative cross-sectional study of Minas Gerais municipalities (SNIS 2018 and IBGE 2017) satisfies Criteria 1, 3, 4, 5, and 6, and passes the plain wording of Criterion 2 because it examines municipal institutional capacity dimensions (financial, technical, operational, and political/planning capacity). However, under the active 2026-10-13 narrow rule-type reading of Criterion 2, it is excluded as E03 (Wrong exposure): its independent variables capture general municipal resource, staffing, equipment, and planning capacity (per capita revenues/expenditures, presence of municipal technical staff, waste vehicles/workers, and binary existence of a municipal sanitation plan/policy combined into PCA factor scores) rather than a rule-type mechanism directly governing household or community service access (such as eligibility screening, administrative burden, documentation/tenure rules, tariff/cost-recovery rules, discretion, enforcement, or utility ownership/regulatory structure).
